cycles.name: Iron Floor
focuses: Build real force in the squat, the hinge and single leg work, with week 1 spent finding your weights.
Start the landing work: quiet, controlled, both legs, every jump stuck and held.
Film your squat and lunge in week 2 and send them to me.

paragraphs: Welcome in, Amirhossein. You told me your legs feel slow on court, especially your speed in the game. Here is what I think is really going on. A padel court is 20 metres long. There is nowhere to sprint. What you are feeling is that you cannot stop fast enough, so you arrive at the ball late and out of position and it feels like slow legs. Stopping is a strength job, and three or four sessions a week on court never builds it.

So this first block builds the floor. Heavy enough squats, proper hinge work, single leg strength, and the landing drills that teach your knee to take all of it. Every session starts with something fast and light so the quick stuff stays sharp while we build underneath it. That short bit at the start is not a warm-up. Do not skip it.

You left your lifts blank on the form, so week 1 is you finding your weights. Read the first note before you start. In week 2 you film one squat set and one lunge set for me, and that is what tells me where you really are before we go heavy in the next block.
outcomes: Working weights found on the squat, RDL and reverse lunge
Week 2 squat and lunge filmed and sent
Quiet, controlled landings on both legs
Stronger brakes: hamstrings, calves and glutes
A gym week that fits around 3-4 padel sessions

cycles.name: Split Steel
cycles.tagline: One leg at a time, heavy
focuses: The heavy block. Real strength on numbers Cycle 1 gave us, led by single leg and split stance work.
Slow eccentrics on the main leg lift, and your first real braking work from a run.

paragraphs: Next block is the heavy one. Once I have seen your film and your numbers we load them properly, and it moves to one leg at a time, because that is how padel is actually played.
One of your legs has been doing more than its share for a while now. Cycle 2 stops letting that happen.
Earn it in these five weeks.

cycles.name: Brake Line
focuses: Deceleration and eccentric force in the directions padel actually uses.
Turning Cycle 2 strength into speed of force: heavy and fast, few reps, full rest.

cycles.name: Spring Steel
focuses: Short ground contacts, stiffness and real plyometrics. Lateral bounds enter here and nowhere earlier.
First step and change of direction: split step into short accelerations, repeated cuts, rotational power.

cycles.name: Third Set
focuses: Repeat that first step and that hard stop while you are tired, over and over, for a match length.
Everything you built held with one heavy and one sharp session a week while the density goes up.

exercises.name: Box Jump
exercises.note: Landing is the whole point here, not how high the box is. Pick a box low enough that you can step back down every time. Never jump down off it.

good: Jump up and land exactly where you took off
Feel the whole foot land quiet and soft
bad: Don't let the knee drift inside the foot when you land

exercises.name: Barbell Back Squat
exercises.note: Stop at parallel, never below. You said deep squats are the one thing your knee does not like, so we simply do not go there. Week 1 is you finding the weight, so start lighter than you think and let the first set tell you. If the station is busy, use the Barbell Box Squat instead and set the box at parallel.

good: Push the floor apart with your feet
Feel it split evenly between quads and glutes
bad: Don't let the knees cave in as you come up

good: Pull the dumbbells back to your hips
Feel the squeeze between the shoulder blades
bad: Don't shrug the shoulders up to your ears

exercises.name: Seated Machine Calf Raise
exercises.note: This one looks small and it is not. With the knee bent you hit the soleus, the deep calf muscle that stops your shin sliding forward. It is doing a real job for your knee and it stays in your program for the whole six months.

good: Push the platform away through the ball of your foot
Feel it low in the calf, near the achilles
bad: Don't bounce out of the bottom

good: Press straight out and hold the line
Feel the side of your trunk fighting the pull
bad: Don't let the ribs flare or the hips twist

days.completionMessage: Hamstrings did the work today and that is the muscle that stops you on court. Expect a bit of stiffness tomorrow, that is normal.

exercises.name: Barbell Romanian Deadlift
exercises.note: Week 1 is calibration on this one too. Go by the stretch, not by how far down the bar goes. Stop where your back would start to round, even if that is only mid shin. Build the range over the block instead of chasing it on day one.

good: Push the hips back toward the wall behind you
Feel the stretch high in the hamstrings
bad: Don't round the back to go lower

exercises.name: Machine Seated Leg Curl
exercises.note: This is the exercise that most serves what you asked me for. Your hamstring is what stops you on court, and a stronger brake is what lets you go harder into the ball. Take three full seconds letting the pad come back up, that slow part is where the work is.

good: Pull the pad down toward the floor
Feel the back of the thigh doing all of it
bad: Don't let the hips lift off the seat

good: Pull your elbows down into your back pockets
Feel the lats, not the biceps
bad: Don't lean back to finish the rep

exercises.name: Ab Wheel Rollout
exercises.note: Put a pad or a folded mat under your knees. Roll out only as far as you can keep a flat back, then come straight back. Short and clean beats long and sagging.

good: Roll out as far as you can hold a flat back
Feel the whole front of your trunk bracing
bad: Don't let the hips sag or the back arch

exercises.name: Snap Down
exercises.note: There is no jump here at all. You drop fast into a strong athletic position and freeze for two seconds. This drill is what earns you the bouncing and side to side jumping later in the plan, so treat it seriously even though it looks easy.

good: Punch the floor and freeze
Feel yourself catch the weight, not sink into it
bad: Don't land stiff-legged or let the knees fall in

exercises.name: Dumbbell Reverse Lunge
exercises.note: Stepping backward instead of forward is deliberate, it is much kinder on the front knee. Control the back leg on the way down, don't just drop into it. If the space is busy, use a Box Step-Up with the box at or below knee height so the front thigh never goes past parallel.

good: Step back long and lower straight down
Feel the front glute and quad take the weight
bad: Don't let the front knee wobble inward

exercises.name: Lateral Step-Down
exercises.note: This is the knee control drill. Keep the box at or below knee height and never let the thigh go past parallel at the bottom. Slow on the way down, three full seconds. Get this right and you earn the side to side jumping work in a few months.

good: Tap the heel to the floor and come straight back up
Feel the side of the hip holding the knee in line
bad: Don't let the knee travel inside the big toe

good: Push the floor away through the big toe
Feel it high in the calf
bad: Don't let the ankle roll out to the little toe side

exercises.name: Copenhagen Plank
exercises.note: This is groin work and padel eats groins. Start with your bottom knee down on the floor if 20 seconds is a grind, that version still counts. Move to the full straight leg version when it feels easy.

good: Push the bench away with the top leg
Feel the inside of the top thigh
bad: Don't let the hips drop or roll backward

cards.title: Week 1 is for finding your weights
cards.body:
You left your lifts blank on the form, so I have not guessed them. The app never gives you a weight. You find it yourself using the RPE number on each exercise. RPE 6 means you could still do about 4 clean reps after the set. RPE 7 means about 3.

For all of week 1, stay at RPE 6 on the Back Squat, the Romanian Deadlift and the Reverse Lunge, even though the card says 7. Start lighter than you think and let the first set tell you. From week 2 you work to the number on the card.

  • New exercise? Go too light on purpose. If it felt easy, add a little next set.
  • Hit all your reps at or under the target RPE? Small jump next week.
  • Missed reps, or it felt harder than the target? Keep the same weight and do it again next week.

Dropping the weight on a bad day is not failure, it is you reading yourself properly. The target is the RPE, never the number on the bar.

cards.title: Film your week 2 squat and lunge
cards.body:
I am not standing next to you, so video is how I coach you. In week 2 only, on Day 1, I want two things filmed from about 45 degrees in front of you.

  • Back Squat, last set only. This one set is the exception to the RPE 7 on the card. Do as many clean reps as you can at parallel and stop at the first rep that slows down, gets shorter, or where your position breaks. Stop about 2 reps before it turns into a grind. Do not go to true failure.
  • Reverse Lunge, one set on each leg, filmed from the front.

That one squat set tells me more than five weeks of logs will. It is what I use to write your heavy block.

Weight stops going up on those two lifts if the videos stop coming. Send them on WhatsApp.

cards.title: Your knee: what's OK and what isn't
cards.body:
Your knee has history and you are asymptomatic now, which is exactly where I want you. So we train it properly and we watch it honestly. Here is the line.

  • Totally fine: burn during a set, a pump, stiffness in the quad or hamstring the next day. Keep training.
  • Not fine: sharp pain at the front of the knee, pain that builds through a set instead of staying flat, swelling by the evening, or the knee giving way.

What to do:

  • Mild and fading? Finish the set and write it in your log.
  • Building, or it changes how you move? Stop that exercise, use the swap written on the card, and message me.
  • Sharp, swelling, or giving way? Stop the session and message me before your next one.

Telling me changes your session, it never cancels your training. I will always find you something else to do. So tell me early, not three weeks late.

cards.title: Gym on a padel day
cards.body:
You are on court 3 or 4 days a week, so most gym days will also be padel days. That is normal and it is fine, as long as you get the order right.

  • Padel first, gym after. Always. 3 hours between them minimum, 4 to 6 is ideal.
  • Less than 3 hours? Do the short version of the day (next note), cap the main lift at RPE 6 and skip all the jumping.
  • Gym before padel is never the plan. If the morning is your only slot, do Day 4, never a leg day.

Day 1 and Day 3 never go back to back. Those are your two hard leg days and they need a day between them. Apart from that, move the sessions around your week however your court bookings fall.

cards.title: Short on time? Shrink the day
cards.body:
Your weeks are long and some days you will not have an hour. Never delete a session, shrink it. Here is the 20 minute version of each day, and it counts as a full session in the app.

  • Day 1: 5 min warm-up, Box Jump 3 sets of 4, Back Squat 3 sets of 6.
  • Day 2: 5 min warm-up, Med Ball Rotational Throw 2 sets of 5 each side, Romanian Deadlift 3 sets of 8.
  • Day 3: 5 min warm-up, Snap Down 3 sets of 5, Reverse Lunge 2 sets of 8 each side.

Three short sessions beat two perfect ones and one you skipped. Tick the day off and move on.

cards.title: Week 5 eases off
cards.body:
Weeks 1 to 4 you build. Week 5 you back off on purpose so you go into the heavy block fresh instead of cooked. Same exercises, same days, less of everything.

  • Every Primary and Accessory drops to 2 sets.
  • The jumping and throwing at the start of each session drops to 2 sets.
  • Nothing goes above RPE 6 that week.

The numbers on the cards do not change, I am not rewriting your program. Just take it easy for that one week and keep playing your padel as normal.

cards.title: You said your eating is hit and miss
cards.body:
You are 78 kg and you want to get faster and look better. Both of those are built out of food, and inconsistent eating is the thing most likely to waste these five weeks.

I am not going to give you a diet before I know how you actually eat. For now just do two things every day and tell me how it goes at the check-in.

  • Protein at every meal. A palm-sized portion, three or four times a day. Eggs, chicken, meat, fish, yoghurt, whatever you actually like.
  • Eat something with carbs and protein within an hour after gym or padel. Especially on double days, that is where you are most likely to be running on empty.

Get those two consistent for five weeks and we can build something proper on top of it.

cards.title: Sleep is your slowest lever
cards.body:
Your hours are fine at 7 to 8, but you rated the quality a 5 out of 10. Your stress is low, so sleep is the one recovery input you can actually move.

Try one thing this block, not five. Pick the easiest one for you and do it every night.

  • Phone out of the room, or at least off the bed.
  • Same wake-up time every day, including on your days off.
  • Nothing heavy or caffeinated in the 3 hours before bed.

Tell me at the check-in whether that 5 has moved. If it has not moved by the end of this block, I will not raise your training volume in the next one, because there would be nothing underneath it to recover from the extra work.
